116: class FFmpegSource(threading.Thread):
117:     """Reads frames from an AVFoundation device through ffmpeg; keeps only the latest one.
118:     Reconnects automatically if the device drops out."""
119: 
120:     def __init__(self, key, label, device, out_size, fps, cap_size=None, vf_pre="", extra_in=()):
121:         super().__init__(daemon=True, name=f"src-{key}")
122:         self.key, self.label, self.device = key, label, device
123:         self.w, self.h = out_size
124:         self.fps, self.cap_size = fps, cap_size
125:         self.vf_pre, self.extra_in = vf_pre, list(extra_in)
126:         self.lock = threading.Lock()
127:         self.frame: np.ndarray | None = None
128:         self.frame_time = 0.0
129:         self.count = 0
130:         self.fps_meas = 0.0
131:         self.error = ""
132:         self.running = True
133:         self.proc: subprocess.Popen | None = None
134:         self._stderr: list[str] = []

136:     def _attempts(self):
137:         tries = [(self.cap_size, self.fps)]
138:         if self.cap_size:
139:             tries += [(self.cap_size, 30), ((640, 480), 30), (None, 30)]
140:         seen, out = set(), []
141:         for t in tries:
142:             if t not in seen:
143:                 seen.add(t)
144:                 out.append(t)
145:         return out

147:     def _cmd(self, cap_size, fps):
148:         cmd = [FFMPEG, "-hide_banner", "-loglevel", "error", "-nostdin",
149:                "-f", "avfoundation", "-pixel_format", "bgr0", "-framerate", str(fps)]
150:         if cap_size:
151:             cmd += ["-video_size", f"{cap_size[0]}x{cap_size[1]}"]
152:         cmd += self.extra_in + ["-i", f"{self.device}:none"]
153:         vf = (self.vf_pre + "," if self.vf_pre else "") + (
154:             f"scale={self.w}:{self.h}:force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease,"
155:             f"pad={self.w}:{self.h}:(ow-iw)/2:(oh-ih)/2")
156:         cmd += ["-vf", vf, "-f", "rawvideo", "-pix_fmt", "bgr24", "-"]
157:         return cmd

159:     def _drain(self, pipe):
160:         for line in iter(pipe.readline, b""):
161:             self._stderr = (self._stderr + [line.decode(errors="replace").strip()])[-5:]

163:     def run(self):
164:         attempts, ai, backoff = self._attempts(), 0, 1.0
165:         n = self.w * self.h * 3
166:         while self.running:
167:             cap_size, fps = attempts[min(ai, len(attempts) - 1)]
168:             self._stderr = []
169:             self.proc = subprocess.Popen(self._cmd(cap_size, fps), stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
170:                                          stderr=subprocess.PIPE, bufsize=0)
171:             threading.Thread(target=self._drain, args=(self.proc.stderr,), daemon=True).start()
172:             got = 0
173:             win_start, win_count = time.perf_counter(), 0
174:             buf = bytearray(n)
175:             while self.running:
176:                 mv, r = memoryview(buf), 0
177:                 while r < n:
178:                     k = self.proc.stdout.readinto(mv[r:])
179:                     if not k:
180:                         break
181:                     r += k
182:                 if r < n:
183:                     break
184:                 img = np.frombuffer(bytes(buf), np.uint8).reshape(self.h, self.w, 3)
185:                 t = time.perf_counter()
186:                 with self.lock:
187:                     self.frame, self.frame_time = img, t
188:                     self.count += 1
189:                 got += 1
190:                 self.error = ""
191:                 win_count += 1
192:                 if t - win_start >= 1.0:
193:                     self.fps_meas = win_count / (t - win_start)
194:                     win_start, win_count = t, 0

199:                 ai += 1  # mode not supported -> try the next fallback right away
200:                 continue
201:             self.error = (self._stderr[-1] if self._stderr else "disconnected")[:90]

203:             time.sleep(backoff)
204:             backoff = min(backoff * 2, 5.0)

206:                 backoff = 1.0

231:         cmd = [FFMPEG, "-hide_banner", "-loglevel", "error", "-y", "-f", "rawvideo", "-pix_fmt", "bgr24",
232:                "-s", f"{w}x{h}", "-r", str(fps), "-i", "-"]
233:         if codec == "hw":
234:             cmd += ["-c:v", "h264_videotoolbox", "-b:v", bitrate, "-allow_sw", "1"]
235:         else:
236:             cmd += ["-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "veryfast", "-crf", str(crf)]
237:         cmd += ["-pix_fmt", "yuv420p", "-movflags", "+faststart", str(path)]
238:         self.proc = subprocess.Popen(cmd, stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
239:         self.q: queue.Queue = queue.Queue(maxsize=120)
240:         self.dropped = 0
241:         self.t = threading.Thread(target=self._loop, daemon=True)
242:         self.t.start()

244:     def _loop(self):
245:         while (item := self.q.get()) is not None:
246:             try:
247:                 self.proc.stdin.write(item)
248:             except (BrokenPipeError, ValueError):
249:                 break

251:     def write(self, frame: np.ndarray):
252:         try:
253:             self.q.put_nowait(frame.tobytes())
254:         except queue.Full:
255:             self.dropped += 1

257:     def close(self) -> str:
258:         self.q.put(None)
259:         self.t.join()
260:         try:
261:             self.proc.stdin.close()
262:         except Exception:
263:             pass
264:         err = self.proc.stderr.read()
265:         self.proc.wait(timeout=60)
266:         return err.decode(errors="replace").strip()

528:     def apply_pending_fps(self):

536:             was_paused, prev = self.state == "paused", self.clip.idx
537:             self.clip.event("split", f"fps change -> {new}, continues in clip {prev + 1:03d}")

561:     def handle_key(self, k: str):
562:         if k in ("q", "esc"):
563:             self.running = False
564:         elif k == " ":
565:             if self.state == "idle":
566:                 self.start_clip()
567:             elif self.state == "recording":
568:                 self.state = "paused"
569:                 self.clip.event("pause")
570:                 self.say("PAUSED")
571:             else:
572:                 self.state = "recording"
573:                 self.clip.event("resume")
574:                 self.say("RESUMED")
575:         elif k == "n":
576:             self.finish_clip()
577:             self.start_clip()
578:         elif k in ("y", "x"):
579:             if self.clip:
580:                 self.finish_clip("success" if k == "y" else "fail")
581:             else:
582:                 self.say("no clip open - press SPACE to start one")
583:         elif k == "e":
584:             self.finish_clip()
585:         elif k == "m":
586:             if self.clip:
587:                 n = sum(e["type"] == "marker" for e in self.clip.events) + 1
588:                 self.clip.event("marker", f"marker {n}")
589:                 self.last_marker = f"marker {n} @ {fmt_dur(self.clip.video_time)}"
590:                 self.say(self.last_marker)
591:             else:
592:                 self.say("markers need an open clip")
593:         elif k == "s":
594:             self.snapshot()
595:         elif k in ("+", "=", "-", "_"):
596:             cur = self.pending_fps or self.fps
597:             i = self.fps_steps.index(cur) if cur in self.fps_steps else 0
598:             i = min(i + 1, len(self.fps_steps) - 1) if k in "+=" else max(i - 1, 0)
599:             if not self.clip:
600:                 self.fps, self.pending_fps = self.fps_steps[i], None
601:                 self.say(f"output FPS -> {self.fps}")
602:             else:  # applied after 1 s without further presses (avoids tiny clips)
603:                 self.pending_fps, self.pending_until = self.fps_steps[i], time.time() + 1.0
604:                 self.say(f"output FPS -> {self.pending_fps} (new clip in 1 s)")
605:         elif k == "c":
606:             self.color = COLOR_MODES[(COLOR_MODES.index(self.color) + 1) % len(COLOR_MODES)]
607:             self.say(f"color: {self.color}")
608:             self.change_setting("color")
609:         elif k in ("[", "]"):
610:             self.brightness = int(np.clip(self.brightness + (10 if k == "]" else -10), -100, 100))
611:             self.say(f"brightness {self.brightness:+d}")
612:             self.change_setting("brightness")
613:         elif k in (";", "'"):
614:             self.contrast = float(np.clip(self.contrast + (0.1 if k == "'" else -0.1), 0.3, 3.0))
615:             self.say(f"contrast {self.contrast:.1f}")
616:             self.change_setting("contrast")
617:         elif k == "0":
618:             self.color, self.brightness, self.contrast = "normal", 0, 1.0
619:             self.say("color reset")
620:             self.change_setting("reset")
621:         elif k == "l" and self.args.source == "cameras":
622:             self.layout = LAYOUTS[(LAYOUTS.index(self.layout) + 1) % len(LAYOUTS)]
623:             self.say(f"layout: {self.layout}")
624:             self.change_setting("layout")
625:         elif k == "f" and self.args.source == "cameras":
626:             self.focus = (self.focus + 1) % len(self.sources)
627:             self.say(f"focus: {self.sources[self.focus].label}")
628:             self.change_setting("focus")
629:         elif k in ("1", "2", "3") and int(k) <= len(self.sources):
630:             i = int(k) - 1
631:             self.hidden ^= {i}

638:         elif k in ("h", "?"):

654:     # --- rendering ---
655:     def layout_rects(self):
656:         W, H = self.W, self.H - FOOTER_H
657:         vis = [i for i in range(len(self.sources)) if i not in self.hidden] or [0]
658:         g = 6
659:         if self.layout == "row":
660:             cw = W // len(vis)
661:             return [(i, (k * cw + g, g, cw - 2 * g, H - 2 * g)) for k, i in enumerate(vis)], None
662:         if self.layout == "single" or len(vis) == 1:
663:             i = self.focus if self.focus in vis else vis[0]
664:             return [(i, (g, g, W - 2 * g, H - 2 * g))], None
665:         if self.layout == "focus":
666:             f = self.focus if self.focus in vis else vis[0]
667:             others = [i for i in vis if i != f]
668:             bw = W * 2 // 3
669:             rects = [(f, (g, g, bw - 2 * g, H - 2 * g))]
670:             sh = H // max(1, len(others))
671:             rects += [(i, (bw + g, k * sh + g, W - bw - 2 * g, sh - 2 * g)) for k, i in enumerate(others)]
672:             return rects, None
673:         cw, ch = W // 2, H // 2  # grid: 2x2, last free cell becomes the info panel
674:         cells = [(c % 2 * cw + g, c // 2 * ch + g, cw - 2 * g, ch - 2 * g) for c in range(4)]
675:         rects = [(i, cells[k]) for k, i in enumerate(vis)]
676:         return rects, (cells[len(vis)] if len(vis) < 4 else None)

678:     def render(self):
679:         canvas = np.full((self.H, self.W, 3), 18, np.uint8)
680:         raws, cam_info, now = {}, [], time.perf_counter()
681:         for s in self.sources:
682:             f, ft, cnt = s.latest()
683:             raws[s.key] = f
684:             cam_info.append((cnt, (now - ft) * 1000 if f is not None else -1))
685:         rects, info_rect = self.layout_rects()
686:         screen = self.args.source == "screen"
687:         for i, (x, y, w, h) in rects:
688:             s = self.sources[i]
689:             f, ft, _ = s.latest()
690:             cv2.rectangle(canvas, (x, y), (x + w, y + h), (0, 0, 0), -1)
691:             if f is None or now - ft > 2.0:
692:                 msg = "NO SIGNAL - reconnecting" if f is None or s.error else "STALLED"
693:                 put_text(canvas, msg, (x + w // 2, y + h // 2), 0.8, (120, 140, 255), 2, None, anchor="center")
694:                 if s.error:
695:                     put_text(canvas, s.error, (x + w // 2, y + h // 2 + 30), 0.45, (150, 150, 150), 1, None,
696:                              anchor="center")
697:             else:
698:                 fit_into(canvas, apply_color(f, self.color, self.brightness, self.contrast), (x, y, w, h))
699:             if not screen:
700:                 put_text(canvas, f"{i + 1}  {s.label}", (x + 12, y + 26), 0.65, (255, 255, 255), 1, (20, 20, 20))
701:                 put_text(canvas, f"{s.fps_meas:4.1f} fps", (x + w - 10, y + 26), 0.5, (170, 230, 170), 1,
702:                          (20, 20, 20), anchor="right")
703:         if info_rect:
704:             self.draw_info(canvas, info_rect)
705:         self.draw_footer(canvas)
706:         return canvas, raws, cam_info

774:     def run(self):
775:         a = self.args
776:         print("NEX Arm recorder")
777:         self.build_sources()
778:         for s in self.sources:
779:             s.start()
780:         keys = TerminalKeys()
781:         preview = not a.no_preview
782:         win = "NEX Arm recorder"
783:         if preview:
784:             cv2.namedWindow(win, cv2.WINDOW_NORMAL)
785:             pw = a.preview_width
786:             cv2.resizeWindow(win, pw, int(pw * self.H / self.W))
787: 
788:         # wait (max 8 s) for every camera to deliver a frame before the first clip starts
789:         t0 = time.time()
790:         while time.time() - t0 < 8 and not all(s.latest()[0] is not None for s in self.sources):
791:             if preview:
792:                 cv2.waitKey(50)
793:             else:
794:                 time.sleep(0.05)
795:         for s in self.sources:
796:             if s.latest()[0] is None:
797:                 print(f"  ! {s.label}: no frames yet ({s.error or 'waiting'})")
798: 
799:         print(f"  output: {self.W}x{self.H} @ {self.fps} fps, {a.codec}, -> {Path(a.out).resolve()}")
800:         print("  hotkeys: SPACE pause/resume  n next clip  y/x success/fail  m marker  s snapshot  "
801:               "+/- fps  c color  l layout  t timestamp  h help  q quit")
802:         if keys.ok:
803:             print("  (hotkeys also work here in the terminal)")
804:         if not a.idle:
805:             self.start_clip()
806: 
807:         signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, lambda *_: setattr(self, "running", False))
808:         signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, lambda *_: setattr(self, "running", False))
809:         next_tick = time.perf_counter()
810:         self.composite = np.zeros((self.H, self.W, 3), np.uint8)
811:         try:
812:             while self.running:
813:                 now = time.perf_counter()
814:                 if now >= next_tick:
815:                     period = 1.0 / self.fps
816:                     lag = int((now - next_tick) / period)
817:                     if lag > self.fps:  # stalled > 1 s: resync instead of padding
818:                         lag, next_tick = 0, now
819:                     self.composite, raws, cam_info = self.render()
820:                     if self.state == "recording" and self.clip:
821:                         self.clip.write(self.composite, raws, cam_info, 1 + lag)
822:                     next_tick += period * (1 + lag)
823:                     if preview:
824:                         cv2.imshow(win, self.preview_frame(self.composite))
825:                 if preview:
826:                     k = cv2.waitKey(1)
827:                     if k != -1:
828:                         k &= 0xFF
829:                         self.handle_key("esc" if k == 27 else chr(k))
830:                     if cv2.getWindowProperty(win, cv2.WND_PROP_VISIBLE) < 1:
831:                         self.running = False
832:                 else:
833:                     time.sleep(max(0.0, min(0.01, next_tick - time.perf_counter())))
834:                 while (k := keys.get()) is not None:
835:                     self.handle_key(k)
836:                 self.apply_pending_fps()
837:                 if a.duration and self.clip and self.clip.video_time >= a.duration:
838:                     self.say(f"duration {a.duration}s reached")
839:                     self.running = False
840:         finally:
841:             self.finish_clip(quiet=True)
842:             for s in self.sources:
843:                 s.stop()
844:             keys.restore()
845:             if preview:
846:                 cv2.destroyAllWindows()
847:                 cv2.waitKey(1)
848:             self.print_summary()

49: ## Architecture (`src/lerobot/`)
50: 
51: - **`scripts/`** — CLI entry points (`lerobot-train`, `lerobot-eval`, `lerobot-record`, etc.), mapped in `pyproject.toml [project.scripts]`.
52: - **`configs/`** — Dataclass configs parsed by draccus. `train.py` has `TrainPipelineConfig` (top-level). `policies.py` has `PreTrainedConfig` base. Polymorphism via `draccus.ChoiceRegistry` with `@register_subclass("name")` decorators.
53: - **`policies/`** — Each policy in its own subdir. All inherit `PreTrainedPolicy` (`nn.Module` + `HubMixin`) from `pretrained.py`. Factory with lazy imports in `factory.py`.
54: - **`processor/`** — Data transformation pipeline. `ProcessorStep` base with registry. `DataProcessorPipeline` / `PolicyProcessorPipeline` chain steps.
55: - **`datasets/`** — `LeRobotDataset` (episode-aware sampling + video decoding) and `LeRobotDatasetMetadata`.
56: - **`envs/`** — `EnvConfig` base in `configs.py`, factory in `factory.py`. Each env subclass defines `gym_kwargs` and `create_envs()`.
57: - **`robots/`, `motors/`, `cameras/`, `teleoperators/`** — Hardware abstraction layers.
58: - **`types.py`** and **`configs/types.py`** — Core type aliases and feature type definitions.

61: 
62: - **`tests/`** — Pytest suite organized by module. Fixtures in `tests/fixtures/`, mocks in `tests/mocks/`. Hardware tests use skip decorators from `tests/utils.py`. E2E tests via `Makefile` write to `tests/outputs/`.
63: - **`.github/workflows/`** — CI: `quality.yml` (pre-commit), `fast_tests.yml` (base deps, every PR), `full_tests.yml` (all extras + E2E + GPU, post-approval), `latest_deps_tests.yml` (daily lockfile upgrade), `security.yml` (TruffleHog), `release.yml` (PyPI publish on tags).
64: - **`docs/source/`** — HF documentation (`.mdx` files). Per-policy READMEs, hardware guides, tutorials. Built separately via `docs-requirements.txt` and CI workflows.
65: - **`examples/`** — End-user tutorials and scripts organized by use case (dataset creation, training, hardware setup).
66: - **`docker/`** — Dockerfiles for user (`Dockerfile.user`) and CI (`Dockerfile.internal`).
67: - **`benchmarks/`** — Performance benchmarking scripts.
68: - **Root files**: `pyproject.toml` (single source of truth for deps, build, tool config), `Makefile` (E2E test targets), `uv.lock`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` & `README.md` (general information).
69: 
70: ## Notes
71: 
72: - **Mypy is gradual**: strict only for `lerobot.envs`, `lerobot.configs`, `lerobot.optim`, `lerobot.model`, `lerobot.cameras`, `lerobot.motors`, `lerobot.transport`. Add type annotations when modifying these modules.
73: - **Optional dependencies**: many policies, envs, and robots are behind extras (e.g., `lerobot[aloha]`). New imports for optional packages must be guarded or lazy. See `pyproject.toml [project.optional-dependencies]`.

169: ## 5. Data collection tips (beginner → reliable policy)
170: 
171: Good data beats clever models. Adopt these defaults and deviate only with evidence.
172: 
173: ### 5.1 Setup & ergonomics
174: 
175: - **Fix the rig and cameras** before touching the software. If the rig vibrates or the operator gets frustrated, fix that first — more bad data won't help.
176: - **Lighting matters more than resolution.** Diffuse, consistent light. Avoid moving shadows.
177: - **"Can you do the task from the camera view alone?"** If no, your cameras are wrong. Fix before recording.
178: - Enable **action interpolation** for rollouts when available for smoother trajectories.
179: 
180: ### 5.2 Practice before you record
181: 
182: - Do 5–10 demos without recording. Build a deliberate, repeatable strategy.
183: - Hesitant or inconsistent demos teach the model hesitation.
184: 
185: ### 5.3 Quality over speed
186: 
187: Deliberate, high-quality execution beats fast sloppy runs. Optimize for speed only **after** strategy is dialed in — never trade quality for it.
188: 
189: ### 5.4 Consistency within and across episodes
190: 
191: Same grasp, approach vector, and timing. Coherent strategies are much easier to learn than wildly varying movements.
192: 
193: ### 5.5 Start small, then extend (the golden rule)
194: 
195: - **First 50 episodes = constrained version** of the task: one object, fixed position, fixed camera setup, one operator.
196: - Train a quick ACT model. See what fails.
197: - **Then add diversity** along one axis at a time: more positions → more lighting → more objects → more operators.
198: - Don't try to collect the "perfect dataset" on day one. Iterate.
199: 
200: ### 5.6 Policy choice for beginners
201: 
202: - **Laptop / first time / want results fast → ACT.** Works surprisingly well, trains fast even on a laptop GPU.
203: - **Bigger GPU / language-conditioned / multi-task → SmolVLA.** Unfreezing the vision encoder (see §7) is a big win here.
204: - Defer π0 / π0.5 / Wall-X / X-VLA until you have a proven ACT baseline and a 20+ GB GPU.
205: 
206: ### 5.7 Recommended defaults for your first task
207: 
208: | Setting          | Value                                                                                                                                                 |
209: | ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
210: | Episodes         | **50** to start, scale to 100–300 after first training                                                                                                |
211: | Episode length   | 20–45 s (shorter is fine for grasp/place)                                                                                                             |
212: | Reset time       | 10 s                                                                                                                                                  |
213: | FPS              | 30                                                                                                                                                    |
214: | Cameras          | **2 cameras recommended**: 1 fixed front + 1 wrist. Multi-view often outperforms single-view. A single fixed camera also works to keep things simple. |
215: | Task description | Short, specific, action-phrased sentence                                                                                                              |
216: 
217: ### 5.8 Troubleshooting signal
218: 
219: - Policy fails at one specific stage → record 10–20 more episodes **targeting that stage**.
220: - Policy flaps / oscillates → likely inconsistent demos, or need more training; re-record worst episodes (use **←** to redo).
221: - Policy ignores the object → camera framing or lighting issue, not a model issue.
222: 
223: See also: [What makes a good dataset](https://huggingface.co/blog/lerobot-datasets#what-makes-a-good-dataset).

227: ## 6. Which policy should I train?
228: 
229: Match the policy to the user's **GPU memory** and **time budget**. Numbers below come from an internal profiling run (one training update per policy). They are **indicative only** — see caveats.
230: 
231: ### 6.1 Profiling snapshot (indicative)
232: 
233: All policies typically train for **5–10 epochs** (see §7).
234:

236: 
237: | Policy      | Batch | Update (ms) | Peak GPU mem (GB) | Best for                                                                                         |
238: | ----------- | ----: | ----------: | ----------------: | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
239: | `act`       |     4 |    **83.9** |          **0.94** | First-time users, laptops, single-task. Fast and reliable.                                       |
240: | `diffusion` |     4 |       168.6 |              4.94 | Multi-modal action distributions; needs mid-range GPU.                                           |
241: | `smolvla`   |     1 |       357.8 |              3.93 | Language-conditioned, multi-task, small VLA. **Unfreeze vision encoder for big gains** (see §7). |

247: **Critical caveats:**

249: - **Optimizer:** measured with **SGD**. LeRobot's default is **AdamW**, which keeps extra optimizer state → **peak memory will be noticeably higher** with the default, especially for `pi0`, `pi05`, `wall_x`, `xvla`.

254: - **< 8 GB VRAM (laptop, 3060, M-series Mac):** → `act`. Maybe `diffusion` if you have ~6–8 GB free.

257: - **80 GB (A100/H100):** → any, with healthy batch. `pi05`, `xvla`, `wall_x` become comfortable.

262: ## 7. How long should I train?
263: 
264: Robotics imitation learning usually converges in a **few epochs over the dataset**, not hundreds of thousands of raw steps. Think **epochs first**, then translate to steps.
265: 
266: ### 7.1 Rule of thumb
267: 
268: - **Typical total: 5–10 epochs.** Start at 5, eval, then decide if more helps.
269: - Very small datasets (< 30 episodes) may want slightly more epochs — but first, **collect more data**.
270: - VLAs with a pretrained vision backbone typically need **fewer** epochs than training from scratch.
271: 
272: ### 7.2 Steps ↔ epochs conversion
273: 
274: ```
275: total_frames     = sum of frames over all episodes      # e.g. 50 eps × 30 fps × 30 s ≈ 45,000
276: steps_per_epoch  = ceil(total_frames / batch_size)
277: total_steps      = epochs × steps_per_epoch
278: ```
279: 
280: Examples for `--batch_size=8`:
281: 
282: | Dataset size            |  Frames | Steps / epoch | 5 epochs | 10 epochs |
283: | ----------------------- | ------: | ------------: | -------: | --------: |
284: | 50 eps × 30 s @ 30 fps  |  45,000 |        ~5,625 |      28k |       56k |
285: | 100 eps × 30 s @ 30 fps |  90,000 |       ~11,250 |      56k |      113k |
286: | 300 eps × 30 s @ 30 fps | 270,000 |       ~33,750 |     169k |      338k |
287: 
288: Pass the resulting total with `--steps=<N>`; eval at intermediate checkpoints (`outputs/train/.../checkpoints/`).
289: 
290: ### 7.3 Per-policy starting points (single-task, ~50 episodes)
291: 
292: | Policy         | Batch | Steps (first run) | Notes                                                             |
293: | -------------- | ----: | ----------------: | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
294: | `act`          |  8–16 |           30k–80k | Usually converges under 50k for single-task.                      |
295: | `diffusion`    |  8–16 |          80k–150k | Benefits from longer training than ACT.                           |
296: | `smolvla`      |   4–8 |           30k–80k | Pretrained VLM → converges fast.                                  |
297: | `pi0` / `pi05` |   1–4 |           30k–80k | Memory-bound; use gradient accumulation for effective batch ≥ 16! |
298: 
299: ### 7.4 Batch size guidance
300: 
301: - **Bigger batch is preferable** for stable gradients on teleop data.
302: - If GPU memory is the bottleneck, use **gradient accumulation** to raise _effective_ batch without raising peak memory.
303: - Scale **learning rate** gently with batch; most LeRobot defaults work fine for a 2–4× batch change.
304: 
305: ### 7.5 Scale LR schedule & checkpoints with `--steps`
306: 
307: LeRobot's default schedulers (e.g. SmolVLA's cosine decay) use `scheduler_decay_steps=30_000`, which is sized for long training runs. When you shorten training (e.g. 5k–10k steps on a small dataset), **scale the scheduler down to match** — otherwise the LR stays near the peak and never decays. Same for checkpoint frequency.
308: 
309: ```bash
310: lerobot-train ... \
311:   --steps=5000 \
312:   --policy.scheduler_decay_steps=5000 \
313:   --save_freq=5000
314: ```
315: 
316: Rule of thumb: set `scheduler_decay_steps ≈ steps`, and `save_freq` to whatever granularity you want for eval (e.g. every 1k–5k steps). Match `scheduler_warmup_steps` proportionally if your run is very short.
317: 
318: ### 7.6 SmolVLA: unfreeze the vision encoder for real gains
319: 
320: SmolVLA ships with `freeze_vision_encoder=True`. Unfreezing usually **improves performance substantially** on specialized tasks, at the cost of more VRAM and slower steps. Enable with:
321: 
322: ```bash
323: lerobot-train ... --policy.type=smolvla \
324:   --policy.freeze_vision_encoder=false \
325:   --policy.train_expert_only=false
326: ```
327: 
328: ### 7.7 Signals to stop / keep going
329: 
330: - Train loss plateaus → stop, save a Hub checkpoint.
331: - Train loss still dropping and you're under 10 epochs → keep going.

335: ## 8. Evaluation & benchmarks
336: 
337: Two flavors of evaluation:
338: 
339: ### 8.1 Real-robot eval (SO-101, etc.)
340: 
341: Reuse `lerobot-record` with `--policy.path` to run the trained policy on-robot and save the run as an eval dataset. Convention: prefix the dataset with `eval_`.
342: 
343: ```bash
344: lerobot-record \
345:   --robot.type=so101_follower --robot.port=<FOLLOWER_PORT> --robot.id=my_follower \
346:   --robot.cameras="{ front: {type: opencv, index_or_path: 0, width: 640, height: 480, fps: 30}}" \
347:   --dataset.repo_id=${HF_USER}/eval_my_task \
348:   --dataset.single_task="<same task description used during training>" \
349:   --dataset.num_episodes=10 \
350:   --policy.path=${HF_USER}/act_my_task
351: ```
352: 
353: Report success rate across episodes. Compare to a teleoperated baseline and to an earlier checkpoint to catch regressions.
354: 
355: ### 8.2 Sim-benchmark eval
356: 
357: For policies trained on sim datasets (PushT, Aloha, LIBERO, MetaWorld, RoboCasa, …) use `lerobot-eval` against the matching `env.type`:
358: 
359: ```bash
360: lerobot-eval \
361:   --policy.path=${HF_USER}/diffusion_pusht \
362:   --env.type=pusht \
363:   --eval.n_episodes=50 \
364:   --eval.batch_size=10 \
365:   --policy.device=cuda
366: ```
367: 
368: - Use `--policy.path=outputs/train/.../checkpoints/<step>/pretrained_model` for local checkpoints.
369: - `--eval.n_episodes` should be ≥ 50 for a stable success-rate estimate.
370: - Available envs live in `src/lerobot/envs/`. See [`docs/source/libero.mdx`](./docs/source/libero.mdx), [`metaworld.mdx`](./docs/source/metaworld.mdx), [`robocasa.mdx`](./docs/source/robocasa.mdx), [`vlabench.mdx`](./docs/source/vlabench.mdx) for specific benchmarks.

372: 
373: ### 8.2b Dockerfiles for benchmark eval

23: Supported commands:
24:     CMD 68  — Enter/exit LeRobot bridge mode (slave only)
25:     CMD 96  — Read 6 servo positions (reply: 12 bytes, 6 × int16 LE)
26:     CMD 97  — Write 6 servo positions (12 bytes, sync-write, no reply)
27:     CMD 98  — Enable/disable torque on all 6 servos

73: def build_frame(device_id: int, cmd: int, args: bytes = b"") -> bytes:
74:     length = len(args) + 2
75:     data_raw = bytes([device_id & 0xFF, length & 0xFF, cmd & 0xFF]) + args

80: def parse_frame(data: bytes) -> tuple[int, int, bytes] | None:
81:     """Parse a CommProtocol frame. Returns (id, cmd, args) or None.
82: 
83:     Accepts both the correct full-range checksum and the buggy short checksum
84:     from the master firmware (tx_packet_complete uses rx_packet.elements.length
85:     instead of tx_packet.elements.length).
86:     """
87:     if len(data) < 6 or data[0] != 0xFF or data[1] != 0xFF:
88:         return None
89:     device_id = data[2]
90:     length = data[3]
91:     total = 4 + length
92:     if len(data) < total:
93:         return None
94:     cmd = data[4]
95:     n = length - 2
96:     args = data[5 : 5 + n]
97:     checksum_byte = data[total - 1]
98:     expected_full = (~sum(data[2 : total - 1])) & 0xFF
99:     expected_short = (~sum(data[2:5])) & 0xFF
100:     if checksum_byte != expected_full and checksum_byte != expected_short:
101:         return None
102:     return (device_id, cmd, bytes(args))

# OpenCode

Use this guide as the starting point for work involving OpenCode itself. It
covers the core concepts needed to configure and customize OpenCode, extend it
with plugins, and build integrations with the OpenCode SDK, clients, and API.

Full documentation is available at <https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/>. This overview is
only an index of core concepts. Before answering a question about a topic below,
fetch the URL named in that section and use the full page as the source of
truth. Follow links from that page when the question needs more detail. Fetch
<https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/> first when you need to discover the relevant
documentation page.

A machine-readable documentation index is available at
<https://opencode.ai/v2/llms.txt>.

## Version policy

Always answer for OpenCode V2 unless the user explicitly asks about V1,
legacy OpenCode, or migrating from V1.

Use only <https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/> documentation as the source of truth for V2.
Do not use <https://opencode.ai/docs/>, which documents V1, and do not use
general web search to resolve a V2 documentation question when the V2 docs or
linked pages cover it. The schema served from
<https://opencode.ai/config.json> accepts both V2 fields and deprecated V1
fields. Never recommend a field it marks deprecated. If V2 documentation is
missing or contradictory, state the uncertainty or ask for clarification instead of falling back to V1.

V1 documentation and syntax may be consulted only when the user explicitly
asks about V1 or when needed as migration input. Outputs and recommendations
must still use V2 unless the user specifically requests a V1 result.

## [CLI](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/cli)

For questions about the terminal interface, command-line invocation, `run`,
`mini`, terminal providers, or other CLI behavior, fetch the
[CLI guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/cli) and the relevant page linked from
that section.

CLI and TUI preferences are separate from OpenCode's server and project
configuration. They live in the global `~/.config/opencode/cli.json`, or
`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode/cli.json` when `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is set. There is no
project-local CLI configuration. Set `OPENCODE_CLI_CONFIG_CONTENT` to merge
inline JSON over the global settings. Most preferences can also be changed from
the TUI by pressing `Ctrl+P` and selecting **Open settings**.

### [Settings](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/cli/config)

Fetch the full [CLI settings reference](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/cli/config)
before editing `cli.json`. It documents every terminal-only setting, accepted
values, and examples, including themes, input, sessions, tabs, diffs, alerts,
Mini, keybindings, terminal plugins, and debugging. Do not put these settings
in `opencode.json(c)`.

### [Keybinds](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/cli/keybinds)

Configure keybindings under `keybinds` in `cli.json`. The leader key is the
`keybinds.leader` entry; leader timing is configured separately under
`leader.timeout`. Bindings can use a string, an array of strings, or an object
when event behavior such as `preventDefault` is required. Disable a binding
with `"none"` or `false`.

Never guess a command ID, default binding, or accepted key syntax. Fetch the
full [keybind reference](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/cli/keybinds), which lists
the current IDs and defaults, before answering or editing a binding.

## [OpenCode configuration](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/config)

OpenCode's server and project configuration uses JSON or JSONC. Include the
published schema so the user's editor can validate fields and provide
autocomplete:

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
}
```

Global configuration lives at `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json(c)` and applies
to every project for that user. Project configuration can live in any directory
as `opencode.json(c)` or `.opencode/opencode.json(c)`, including nested packages
in a monorepo.

During ordinary project discovery, OpenCode searches the current Location
directory and every ancestor through the filesystem root, including directories
above the detected project or repository root. It merges direct
`opencode.json(c)` files from the farthest ancestor to the current directory,
then does the same for `.opencode/opencode.json(c)` files. This means every
discovered `.opencode` config overrides every discovered direct config. Global
filesystem configuration has lower precedence than these discovered documents.

Common configuration fields include `model`, `default_agent`, `permissions`,
`agents`, `commands`, `plugins`, `providers`, `mcp`, `skills`, `instructions`,
`references`, `formatter`, and `lsp`.

This configuration is distinct from `cli.json`. Use the
[CLI settings reference](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/cli/config) for terminal
preferences, especially themes and keybindings.

Config changes apply without a restart. OpenCode watches config files and
reloads agents, commands, skills, MCP servers, and plugins after a save. The TUI
does the same for `cli.json`. To force a full reload, use `/reload`. Don't tell
the user to restart OpenCode after editing config.

Do not guess field names or shapes. Fetch the V2 configuration guide and its
linked topic guide as the source of truth, and preserve unrelated settings when
editing an existing file. Keep the published `$schema` URL in configuration
examples, but do not fetch it to determine the V2 configuration shape.

See the [full configuration guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/config) for
every field, examples, config locations, and links to dedicated feature guides.

## [MCP servers](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/mcp-servers)

Configure MCP servers under `mcp.servers`. Prefer the CLI because it preserves
unrelated configuration. Use `--global` when the user asks to set up a service
for themselves without limiting it to the current project; omit it when they
explicitly want project-local configuration.

```sh
opencode mcp add <name> --global --url <remote-url>
opencode mcp list
```

Remote servers use OAuth by default. If `mcp list` reports that a server needs
authentication, tell the user to run `/mcps`, select the server, and sign in.
Do not run `opencode mcp auth` through the shell tool: it starts an interactive
flow whose authorization link can be hidden in background process output.
Use the user-facing MCP interface instead.

Report the server as configured but awaiting sign-in until its connection
status confirms it is connected.

OAuth credentials are stored outside the OpenCode configuration. Do not ask for or
store an API key when the server supports OAuth. Use header-based credentials
only when OAuth is unavailable or the user explicitly requires them, and use an
environment substitution such as `{env:MCP_API_KEY}` instead of writing a
secret into configuration.

## [V1 to V2 migration](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/migrate-v1)

For any request to migrate OpenCode configuration, agents, commands, skills,
plugins, integrations, or other behavior from V1 to V2, read the full
[migration guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/migrate-v1) before acting. In
the repository, its source is `services/www/src/docs/content/migrate-v1.mdx`.

V1 config files and `.opencode/` definitions are intended to remain compatible.
The only intentional breaking changes are the server API and plugin API. Native
V2 config uses more ergonomic shapes, but conversion is optional. When the user
requests conversion, inspect the complete configuration, preserve behavior and
unrelated settings, and apply only the relevant migrations from the guide. For
plugin migrations, fetch and follow both the migration guide and the full
[plugins guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins). If non-API V1
functionality fails in V2, use the `report` skill to file it as a compatibility
bug.

## [Plugins](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins)

For questions about creating, configuring, loading, publishing, or migrating
plugins, fetch the full [plugins guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins)
before answering. Refer to this guide when the user wants to build a plugin. It
covers hooks, transforms, tools, plugin context capabilities, and package
entrypoints. Plugins can also extend the TUI; for those, fetch the
[CLI plugin guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins/cli).
For custom methods and events shared with other plugins or clients, fetch the
[RPC guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins/rpc).

## [Service](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/troubleshooting#check-the-background-service)

OpenCode uses a client-server architecture. Interfaces such as the TUI connect
to a background OpenCode service, which owns sessions, configuration, plugins,
permissions, and tool execution.

OpenCode normally discovers or starts the shared background service
automatically. Restart it only if it is stuck or unhealthy, not to apply
configuration changes:

```sh
opencode service restart
```

Check its status after restarting:

```sh
opencode service status
```

## [API](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/api)

OpenCode exposes an HTTP API from its server. The API is described by an
OpenAPI document available from the running server at `/openapi.json`.

Use OpenCode's built-in `api` command for local requests. It uses the same
discovery and authentication flow as the TUI and may start the background
service when no compatible healthy service is available. It accepts either an
HTTP method and path or an OpenAPI operation ID.

Call an endpoint with an HTTP method and path:

```sh
opencode api get /api/info
```

Pass a request body with `--data` or `-d`, and additional headers with
`--header` or `-H`:

```sh
opencode api post /api/example --data '{"key":"value"}'
opencode api get /api/example --header 'X-Example:value'
```

Request bodies default to `Content-Type: application/json`. When OpenCode is
connected to an explicit server instead of its managed background service, use
the same configured server and authentication context rather than constructing
an unauthenticated request separately.

See the [full API reference](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/api) for available
endpoints, parameters, request bodies, and response schemas. The
raw [OpenAPI specification](https://opencode.ai/v2/openapi.json) is also
available for code generation and other tooling.

## [Client](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/client)

For questions about connecting an application to OpenCode over the network,
fetch the full [client guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/client) before
answering.

`@opencode/client` is the generated TypeScript client for the OpenCode HTTP
API. Its methods and types come from the same contract as the API reference.
The default entrypoint exposes Promise-based resource clients and async
iterables for streaming endpoints. The `@opencode/client/effect` entrypoint
exposes typed Effects, Streams, and decoded OpenCode schema values. Its
`Service` API can discover, start, stop, and authenticate with the local
background service from a Node application.

## [SDK](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/sdk)

For questions about embedding OpenCode directly in an application, fetch the
full [SDK guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/sdk) before answering. The SDK
hosts OpenCode in the application without opening an HTTP listener.

Use the [Effect SDK guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/sdk/effect) for
Effect applications. For Cloudflare Durable Objects, use the
[Cloudflare SDK guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/sdk/cloudflare).

## [Troubleshooting](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/troubleshooting)

OpenCode runs a client and a background server. Start by determining whether a
problem belongs to the client, the shared server, or one project.

- Check the service with `opencode service status` and verify the API with
  `opencode api get /api/info`.
- Compare with `opencode --standalone`, which runs the TUI with a private
  server, to isolate shared-service issues.
- Inspect `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log`. Filter `role=cli` for
  client startup and `role=server` for sessions, providers, plugins,
  permissions, and tools.
- Run one reproduction with `OPENCODE_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG` when normal logs are not
  sufficient.
- Do not delete or edit the database, service registration, or service config
  while diagnosing a problem. Back up persistent data before inspecting it
  with external tools.
- Redact API keys, authorization headers, prompts, file contents, and other
  sensitive data before sharing diagnostics.

See the [full troubleshooting guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/troubleshooting)
for service lifecycle commands, API inspection, log locations, explicit server
connections, issue-reporting details, and local development paths.
